newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says sure Germany can solve budget problems.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says sure Germany can solve budget problems.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday he was confident that Germany could solve its budget problems in 1997 and 1998.
Speaking to the lower house of parliament, Kohl said "I am totally certain that we can master our problems."
Kohl had hoped to make a major stride in slashing its deficits by revaluing Bundesbank official reserves, reaping a windfall profit which could be used to pay down government debts.
The Bundesbank, however, rejected the plan as an attack its independence and a threat to the stability of the euro.
Germany faces an uphill battle in reducing its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product as is required for countries hoping to join European monetary union.
At the end of 1996, the budget overhang stood at 3.8 percent and many private economists expect Bonn to come no closer this year than 3.3 percent or so.
